questions.question: One model handles text and images in a shared token space. What must stay measured per modality?
options: Nothing; sharing guarantees equal quality
Only the total parameter count
The training hardware brand
Quality per modality on domain data
questions.explanation: Shared spaces hide uneven quality. This lesson fuses modalities with reserved ranges.

questions.question: How many image token IDs does image_to_tokens produce for an 8x8 grayscale image?
options: 2, one for each spatial axis
4, one downsampled code for each 4x4 quadrant
16, one for every codebook entry
64, one for every input pixel
questions.explanation: The function iterates over two 4-pixel row blocks and two 4-pixel column blocks. Each quadrant is reduced to a 2x2 patch vector, yielding four codebook IDs.

questions.question: What does quantize_patch return after selecting the nearest CODEBOOK row?
options: The raw L2 distance, so the decoder can rank errors
A text token below VOCAB_TEXT
The winning codebook index shifted by IMG_OFFSET=32
The four-dimensional codebook vector itself
questions.explanation: quantize_patch compares squared L2 distances, keeps the best index k, and returns k + IMG_OFFSET. Image IDs therefore occupy 32..47 rather than colliding with text IDs.

questions.question: What is the ordering of a dataset sequence when make_dataset takes its image-first branch?
options: Text caption, then a raw pixel matrix, with no separator
Only text tokens, because image tokens are targets rather than inputs
An image codebook vector followed by a text string object
<image>, four image tokens, </image>, then the synthetic caption tokens
questions.explanation: With probability 0.4, make_dataset builds [SEP_OPEN] + image_to_tokens(...) + [SEP_CLOSE] + synthesize_caption(...). The other branch places the caption first.

questions.question: How does render represent the separator token SEP_OPEN?
options: As the literal string <image>
As an image code such as i16
As a text word such as w48
It omits separators from the rendered sequence
questions.explanation: render checks t == SEP_OPEN before the numeric ranges and appends '<image>'. SEP_CLOSE is rendered similarly as '</image>'.

questions.question: When does generate stop before reaching max_len?
options: Whenever the sampled token is an image code
When SEP_CLOSE is sampled and at least one text token appears in the output
After exactly four tokens, because every image has four patches
Only when the bigram dictionary has no entry for the previous token
questions.explanation: The loop appends a sampled token, then breaks if it is SEP_CLOSE and any token below VOCAB_TEXT is already present. This permits a completed mixed sequence to terminate early.
